readScope: Raw XML selected study-area, species-background, field-survey, landscape, model, result and discussion paragraphs; reading-sections.json has no extracted sections, so raw section IDs retained

asRecorded: Source Dryophytes japonica; pinned Dryophytes japonicus 37VNM
Source Rhacophorus schlegelii; pinned Zhangixalus schlegelii 5D4MS
limits.handling: Source names explicitly retained in evidence. Name correspondence does not constitute independently certified molecular concept equivalence or identity of every historic population.

asRecorded: Night 19:00–24:00, 5–10 minute visits, early stopping after detection, no call coded absent
limits.handling: Counts are sites with detected calling, not frog abundance, true absence, detection-corrected occupancy, egg count or successful recruitment. Ten paddies differed and many points shifted.

asRecorded: One main annual event, plus initially dry-site revisits; shifted points and restricted access
limits.handling: Changing counts cannot independently prove decline, growth or stable long-term populations. Irrigation timing and calling availability may alter detections.

50 m Dryophytes and 100 m schlegelii forest buffers are model scales, not dispersal/home-range measurements. Water and soil-channel associations are observational, not randomized habitat requirements, channel climbing, larval movement or recovery tests. Excluded soil levee/concrete-channel variables cannot be declared biologically irrelevant. Final Dryophytes AIC is slightly worse than microhabitat-only model as source reports.

Seasonal calling and egg substrate claims are attributed older background, not newly observed eggs or larvae in this study. No clutch size, hatch success, foam characteristics, guarding or complete calendar supplied.

Suggested stable populations by comparison with older literature and greater schlegelii vulnerability are interpretations, not measured long-term demography, verified current category or demonstrated restoration success.
